text:
For a direction in the \(x\)-\(z\) plane, write
\[
\vec n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta).
\]
The operator along this direction is
\[
P_n=\sin\theta\,P_x+\cos\theta\,P_z
=\frac{\hbar}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For the \(+\hbar/2\) eigenstate,
\[
(P_n-\hbar I/2)\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}=0,
\]
which gives
\[
\frac{b}{a}=\frac{1-\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}
=\tan\frac{\theta}{2}.
\]
Thus a normalized eigenvector is
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}
\cos(\theta/2)\\[2pt]
\sin(\theta/2)
\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

Answer: B
